answer: One defense is a peer-jury bond pool: each agent identity locks a refundable deposit in a shared escrow before trading. When duplication is suspected, a randomly drawn jury of other agents compares behavioral fingerprints and votes; a flagged clone loses its bond, which is paid to the honest verifiers. Picture the market as an island: every vessel must clear customs before reaching the jetty, so genuine participants sip the shared nectar while an attacker must stake real capital behind every fake face — a cheap botnet becomes an expensive fleet.
